knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A request from a tenant or occupant does not establish authority. Written approval from the person who controls the building or site is the gate before any height plan is considered.
The hierarchy starts by eliminating the need to work at height. Fall-arrest comes last, only where prevention and positioning are not possible.

The NSW construction guidance requires a safe work method statement where a fall could exceed two metres (NSW-17, confirmed). A glazing certificate, tenancy agreement or parking permit is not the required document.
A condition that cannot be checked is recorded as unknown until a competent person checks it. Saying the glass is safe or compliant overstates what the job has verified.
The lesson states that it grants no licence, certificate or authority to work at height. Passing a quiz is not authority, and the employer's agreement alone does not replace the state rule.

practicalCriteria: Given a job pack, the learner names the person with site authority and records the approval date and scope.
The learner writes a scope that lists included and excluded windows, levels and methods.
The learner records at least three verified facts, separately from at least two unknowns, on the job record.
The learner applies the height hierarchy in writing and states whether a ground-based method can meet the scope.
The learner issues a hold notice when authority is missing and names the person who must resolve it.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately by an assessor using the practical criteria, and a knowledge pass is not presented as practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Completed job pack with the authority record
Written scope with included and excluded items
Job record showing verified facts and unknowns in separate entries
stopWorkCriteria: The learner proceeds to a height plan without written authority from the site controller.
The learner records an unknown as safe or compliant.
The learner schedules height work before the risk assessment is received.
